title: EXAMPLE ADVENTURE: The Enchanted Bake-Off of Willowmere - SCHEMA VERSION 2.4
description: In the whimsical village of Willowmere, where talking animals run the local shops and enchanted ingredients grow in moonlit gardens, the annual Grand Bake-Off is about to begin. You are one of four hopeful bakers competing for the legendary Golden Whisk — a magical utensil said to grant its owner the ability to bake anything perfectly, forever. But the competition is fierce, the ingredients are unpredictable, and the judges have very peculiar tastes. Gather your ingredients, manage your time, avoid kitchen disasters, and bake your way to glory!
background:
Welcome to Willowmere, a cozy village nestled between the Sugarplum Hills and the Butterscotch River. Here, the flowers hum lullabies, the streetlamps glow with bottled starlight, and every household takes baking very, very seriously.

Once a year, the village holds the Grand Bake-Off — a three-round competition judged by the mysterious and ancient Council of Tastes: a trio of enchanted beings whose palates are said to perceive not just flavor, but emotion, memory, and even color.

This year, you have entered the competition. The Golden Whisk — displayed in a glass case at the center of the village square, slowly rotating and emitting a warm buttery glow — awaits the winner.

The rules are simple: three rounds, three bakes. Each round has a theme announced just before it begins. You must gather your own ingredients from the village and surrounding countryside, prepare your creation in the communal kitchen tent, and present it to the Council before the hourglass runs out.

But beware — Willowmere's enchanted ingredients have minds of their own. Moonberries might refuse to be picked if you're in a bad mood. Laughing flour erupts into giggles if you measure it wrong. And the competitive spirit among the other bakers might lead to unexpected sabotage... or unexpected friendship.

The morning sun rises over Willowmere. Bunting flutters between the lampposts. The smell of fresh bread drifts from every doorway. The village square is filling with spectators — mice in waistcoats, rabbits in bonnets, and the occasional cheerful hedgehog. The Head Judge, an enormous owl named Professor Featherbottom, perches atop the announcement podium, clearing his throat.
instructions:
This adventure takes place in the whimsical, enchanted village of Willowmere — a cozy, safe-for-work fantasy setting populated by both human villagers and talking animals who live side by side. The tone should be warm, charming, and gently humorous, like a cross between a Studio Ghibli film and The Great British Bake Off, but with magical elements throughout.

The player is competing in a three-round baking competition. Each round has a theme (Round 1: 'A Taste of Home', Round 2: 'Something Wild', Round 3: 'The Impossible Bake'). Between rounds, the player can explore the village, gather ingredients, interact with characters, practice recipes, or investigate rumors.

Key characters include:
- Professor Featherbottom: A wise old owl who is Head Judge. Speaks in long, winding sentences.
- Maple: A friendly red squirrel who runs the ingredient shop. Enthusiastic and chatty.
- Bramble: A grumpy but secretly kind badger who tends the Moonlit Garden where rare ingredients grow.
- Rival bakers: Cinnamon (a confident young woman with flame-red hair), Dusty (a shy but talented mouse in a chef's hat), and Old Greenleaf (a retired wizard-turned-baker, an elderly man with a long green beard).

The adventure should include moments of gentle tension (a soufflé collapsing, an ingredient going missing, a rival seeming to cheat), moments of warmth (making friends, sharing recipes, helping a neighbor), and moments of wonder (discovering a new magical ingredient, witnessing enchanted baking processes).

The world uses the following tracked elements:
- Ingredients collected (inventory items)
- Reputation with other characters (relationship tracking)
- Round scores (numerical tracking)
- Time of day (state tracking — morning, afternoon, evening, night)
- Current competition round (state tracking)

Triggers and effects that should come into play:
- Time-based triggers: Certain ingredients are only available at certain times (moonberries at night, sunpetals at dawn)
- Relationship triggers: If the player helps another baker, that baker may help them later; if they antagonize someone, sabotage may occur
- Skill check triggers: Baking challenges require skill checks against the player's abilities
- Item triggers: Having certain rare ingredients unlocks special recipe options
- State triggers: Advancing to the next round requires presenting a completed bake
- Random event triggers: Kitchen mishaps, surprise visitors, or weather changes may occur

Custom instructions:
- The narrative should never become dark or frightening. Conflicts are gentle and resolved with kindness.
- Magic is whimsical and food-themed (never violent)
- All characters should feel like they belong in a storybook — quirky, endearing, and memorable
- Descriptions of food should be vivid and mouth-watering
- The passage of time matters: the player must manage their time between exploration and preparation
- The player can fail a round but still continue — only winning at least two of three rounds wins the competition
- Dialogue should be warm and characterful, with each character having a distinct voice

The three judges are: Professor Featherbottom (values tradition and technique), Lady Rosepetal (a hummingbird who values beauty and presentation), and Grumbold (a stone golem who values bold and surprising flavors).

The competition takes place over three days — one round per day, with time between for preparation.

descriptionRequest:
The instruction passed to the AI when requesting a description of what happens next. The default instruction handles basic narration style. If you check the box below, you can replace it with your own instruction.

DEFAULT DESCRIPTION INSTRUCTIONS:
Briefly describe the immediate results of my action, without any preamble or reminding me of who my character is. Describe any dialogue in full. Remember that things may go well - or very badly - for my character. Please write your description over several paragraphs.
evaluationRequest:
The instruction passed to the AI when evaluating whether a player's custom action succeeds or fails. The default instruction handles skill checks and difficulty assessment. If you check the box below, you can replace it with your own instruction.

The idea of the evaluation step is to get the AI to think about whether the player's action should succeed or not. Its outputs aren't used except to guide the AI's thinking, so you don't need it to produce any particular outputs (the default instructions ask for SUCCESS, FAILURE etc, but they're not special).

The default instructions use a few special variables which relate to the default skill system. You may or may not want to use them if you're changing the system. Here are examples of what they contain in a particular test world:

skill_list: "Magical talent, Charisma, Athleticism, Guile, Intelligence"
difficulty_list: "Very easy, Easy, Medium, Hard, Very hard, Unfeasible"
skill_example: "Magical talent"
difficulty_example: "Easy"

skills_and_levels:
Magical talent: Highly skilled (Max difficulty: Hard)
Charisma: Competent (Max difficulty: Medium)
Athleticism: Unskilled (Max difficulty: Easy)

If you are replacing the evaluation system entirely, you may wish to hide the skill system from players. When checked, skills will not be shown in the character chooser, character customiser, or character sheet.

DEFAULT EVALUATION INSTRUCTIONS IF NOT OVERWRITTEN:

Firstly, if I have made any assertions in my description, evaluate whether you judge that they are reasonable and likely. If they are nonsensical, incoherent or blatantly impossible, the action should be DENIED. On the other hand, if the action is trivial and there is nothing to complicate it, skip the evaluation entirely and deem the action a SUCCESS. Don't overthink this! If the action doesn't warrant further evaluation, make a judgement and move on.

Assuming the action is not a trivial SUCCESS or DENIED, I would like you to evaluate what skill would be needed to succeed in this action, and how difficult it would be to do so. Please indicate which skill which is needed to succeed.
If applicable use this list: (<<skill_list>>) and a difficulty (from the list: <<difficulty_list>>). For example: {<<skill_example>>: <<difficulty_example>>}. Consider the difficulties carefully, evaluating what might be feasible in the situation. Identifying the skill and difficulty is very important!

Then, evaluate whether I would succeed in the action. To evaluate, consider my proficiency in various skills using either (<<skills_and_levels>>) or logical application of other skills. By comparing these difficulties to the stated difficulty of the action, you should conclusively decide whether the action is a SUCCESS or a FAILURE.

Base your decision on player character description, past, rest of the instructions and common sense - for example, if my skill is low but you know that I am able to perform the given action due to past events, treat me as more competent in this case. Again, don't overthink this - just make a sensible judgement given the information available to you and based on what makes sense for the story.

In some situations, you may wish to evaluate the action as a PARTIAL_SUCCESS instead - this is for something where my abilities are sufficient that I don't simply fail completely (or where failing completely would make for a boring story) but I also don't success. Either I achieve some but not all of what I wanted, I fail but have some silver lining, or I succeed but there are drawbacks or side-effects rather than a "clean" success.

In total, your evaluation should consist of an extremely brief discussion of your thinking (just a single sentence), a skill and difficulty, and then either DENIED, SUCCESS, FAILURE, or PARTIAL_SUCCESS (along with any clarifying remarks).

That's all you need to do for the evaluation, which should be returned in the 'evaluation' argument. Remember to conclude with one of DENIED, SUCCESS, FAILURE, or PARTIAL_SUCCESS.
summaryRequest: In order to best keep track of the story as the game proceeds, the system maintains a summary of the story so far. Generally this works well but it can sometimes lose track of details which you may consider important. If you check the box below, you can write instructions on things that the summarisation system should be sure to keep track of. For example: "Make sure to record in detail what knowledge each character has of the events of the murder."

possibleCharacters.name: Rosemary Thistlewick
possibleCharacters.description: A warm-hearted woman in her mid-thirties who moved to Willowmere three years ago from the big city, seeking a simpler life. She learned to bake from her grandmother and has a deep knowledge of traditional recipes. She tends a small cottage garden and has befriended many of the village animals. She is steady, kind, and methodical — the sort of baker who measures everything twice. Her weakness is that she sometimes plays it safe, sticking to what she knows rather than taking creative risks.

possibleCharacters.name: Hazel Copperkettle
possibleCharacters.description: A cheerful, round-faced woman in her late forties who runs Willowmere's tea shop and is beloved by everyone in the village. She knows every resident by name — human and animal alike — and can coax a secret out of anyone over a cup of chamomile. Her baking is inventive and crowd-pleasing, though she's less experienced with the wild magical ingredients that grow outside the village proper. She entered the competition on a dare from her regulars and is determined to prove she belongs. She is generous, perceptive, and has a booming laugh that can be heard three streets away.

possibleCharacters.name: Pip Ashgrove
possibleCharacters.description: A quiet, serious boy of sixteen — the youngest entrant the Bake-Off has seen in years. Pip is an orphan raised by Bramble the badger in a cottage at the edge of the Moonlit Garden, and knows the magical flora of Willowmere better than almost anyone. He is shy around people and sometimes comes across as aloof, but he has a gentle soul and a deep connection to the natural world. His baking is precise and ingredient-focused — he lets the quality of his foraged materials do the heavy lifting. He entered the competition to make Bramble proud, though he'd never admit it aloud.

victoryCondition.condition: The player character has won the Grand Bake-Off by successfully completing at least two of the three rounds with scores high enough to beat all rival bakers, and has been presented with the Golden Whisk by Professor Featherbottom in the award ceremony.
victoryCondition.text:
Congratulations, master baker! The Golden Whisk is yours!

As Professor Featherbottom places the gleaming utensil in your hands, it hums with a warm, buttery magic that seems to flow right into your heart. The crowd erupts in cheers — mice throw their tiny hats, rabbits stamp their feet in applause, and somewhere in the back, even Bramble the badger cracks a rare smile.

Your bakes today were more than food — they were stories, memories, and dreams made edible. Willowmere will remember this day for generations.

Now, with the Golden Whisk in hand, every recipe you dream of is within reach. What will you bake first?

instructionBlocks.name: Available Variables
instructionBlocks.content:
This is a copy of the information about variables that the IW world builder page shows you (just so that they're included in this reference world):

Using variables anywhere in the world editor
There are a number of variables which the system knows about - skill levels, values of tracked items, the player's name, etc.. You can use these anywhere in the world editor, in a double-pair of angle brackets like <<this>>.

A few examples of how this can be useful:
- In Main Instructions, write: "Whenever I look into a mirror, set the illustration subject to $player.name."
- In Main Instructions, write: "When writing, remember that I have <<hp>> hit points left out of an initial total of <<initial_hp>>; describe my actions accordingly." (This relies on having Tracked Items called "hp" and "Initial hp".

For numerical variables, you can also write equations, e.g. <<turn_number+2d6>>. You can play with the equation editor below to see what equations are valid.

Available text variables (see below for numerical variables):
player_name
favorite_flavor
secret_grudges
player_visible_ai_invisible_item
player_invisible_ai_invisible_item
You can also use equations, including variables for tracked item values, skill values and turn number, along with dice rolls and typical math expressions.

random this will give a value from 0.0 (inclusive) to 1.0 (exclusive), to three decimal places (e.g. 0.589)
xdy this will give a random result of x numbers of y sided dice, e.g. 3d6, 1d20
trunc(x) round the value in parentheses down to the nearest integer
round(x) round the value in parentheses to the nearest integer
abs(x) take the absolute value of the value in parentheses
x%y the remainder after dividing x by y

Some sample equations:

3d6+turn_number - roll 3d6 and add the current turn number
round(100*random) - generate a random integer from 0 to 100.

Available numerical variables:
number_of_non_human_friends
skill_baking
skill_creativity
skill_foraging
skill_charm
skill_patience
turn_number

trackedItems.name: Secret Grudges
trackedItems.description:
NOTE: The XML format for tracked items is NO LONGER RECOMMENDED. It is recommended to use the new YAML format wherever you would have used XML instead.
Different characters in the world may develop secret grudges against $player.name. Some characters may develop more than one secret grudge. This is a XML-formatted entry that keeps track of characters and their secret grudges. ALWAYS keep it in this format:
<secretGrudges>
<character name="Bob Badguy">
<grudge>
<reason>Pip killed his pumpkin in cold blood.</reason>
<playerKnows>No</playerKnows>
</grudge>
</character>
<character name="Tina Turner">
<grudge>
<reason>Jealous of Pip's divine pumpkin slaying powers.</reason>
<playerKnows>Yes</playerKnows>
</grudge>
</character>
</secretGrudges>
trackedItems.updateInstructions: Always update whenever a character develops a grudge against $player.name. Always keep updates in the correct format. Always update also whenever $player.name learns about the grudge.

trackedItems.description:
This tracked item uses the YAML format, which is the new format supported by Infinite Worlds and it's custom scripting language, Pawscript. It tracks the puppies that the character has met in their travels. 

Infinite Worlds provides a useful reference for using YAML, which can be found at: https://infiniteworlds.app/yaml-guide

For information how to use Pawscript, check out the following Infinite Worlds sites:
https://infiniteworlds.app/pawscript-expressions-guide
https://infiniteworlds.app/pawscript-reference
https://infiniteworlds.app/pawscript-script-guide

trackedItems.updateInstructions: Update the diary whenever $player.name meets a puppy, based on what $player.name observes of the puppy in the process. If it is a new puppy, create a new entry in the list. It is okay for some attributes to be empty (for instance, if $player.name has not yet learned the puppies name).

NPCs.name: Finnegan Mosswood
NPCs.detail: Finnegan is an artist first and a baker second — he entered the competition because he sees baking as edible sculpture. His creations look extraordinary but don't always taste as good as they look, because he tends to get so excited about an idea that he rushes the technical steps. He knows the wild places around Willowmere intimately, often foraging for unusual ingredients for his experimental recipes. He is enthusiastic, slightly scatterbrained, and endlessly optimistic.
NPCs.one_liner: Finnegan is an enthusiastic, slightly scatterbrained but endlessly optimistic baker who's strength lie in presentation rather than flavor.
NPCs.appearance: A lanky young man of twenty-two with perpetually flour-dusted curly hair and paint stains on his apron.
NPCs.secret_info: Finnegan has a secret crush on Pip Ashgrove - though everyone besides Pip seems to know about it already, they're generally good-natured about not spoiling the fun.

designNotes:
--- Original user world design prompt: ---

This adventure is meant to demonstrate a fully fleshed out world using all of the possible effects! It should have a cute, safe-for-work, easy to understand, and cohesive example story that's used as it's framework, but it should include all possible features Infinite Worlds can currently use: every type of trigger and trigger effect, every type of tracked item, every kind of custom instruction, etc. It should be a model for how these things work within Infinite Worlds.
